item.title: Lilu King files constitutional proceedings to regain refugee status
item.description: Lilu King, also known as Mohamed Ali Ahmed Elmushraty, filed constitutional proceedings seeking to regain refugee status in Malta, arguing that deportation to Tunisia could see him returned to Libya, where he claims he was tortured. The application, lodged by lawyers Franco Debono, Jos Herrera, Marion Camilleri and Martina Herrera, challenges the International Protection Agencys refusal to restore his status, citing rights against torture and to a fair trial. He was granted refugee status in December 2015 before the agency ruled in May 2023 that it had expired under subsidiary legislation.

item.title: Stivalas twin 15-storey Sliema hotels back before the planning tribunal
item.description: Both 15-storey hotels built by developer Carlo Stivala a block apart on the Strand near the Sliema Ferries are back before the planning tribunal after the Court of Appeal overturned the tribunals decisions on each. Judge Mark Simiana found the tribunal had reshaped the buildings without showing the altered plans to objectors and had waved through works on one for the wrong reasons. The Triq il-Lunzjata hotel is already operating as the Sliema Centric Hotel above the Piccolo Padre restaurant, whose awning was cleared from the pavement and road earlier this year, while the Triq San Vinenz project replaces the former Sliema Labour Party club and is planned to rise 14 floors to a rooftop pool.

item.title: Environment coalition warns of fresh protests over proposed ODZ amnesty
item.description: The ustizzja gal Artna coalition condemned Prime Minister Robert Abelas comments reviving the idea of an amnesty for development illegalities, saying the groups are ready to return to the streets if it goes ahead. Abela said in a Sunday interview he was considering an amnesty applying to developments in ODZ areas, including illegal residences, while excluding commercial illegalities. The proposal was part of the July 2025 planning reform that triggered widespread protests before being shelved. The coalition said it would not agree to any ODZ amnesty and called the renewed talk a sign of a lack of commitment to just solutions.

item.title: Farrugia board pay row escalates as MEA rejects claims and an MP seeks a privilege ruling
item.description: The Malta Employers Association has rejected claims by Labour MP Nigel Vella that its former director general Joseph Farrugia holds or held five government-remunerated board positions worth about 20,000 a year, saying the figures are inflated and that Farrugia was never appointed to the Malta Development Bank board and received no payments from it. The dispute escalated after Farrugia returned his ie ir-Repubblika honour following Yorgen Fenechs acquittal, with Vella saying in parliament that Farrugia had called him and Neville Gafa clowns on Facebook and requesting a ruling from the Speaker over an alleged breach of parliamentary privilege.

item.title: Consumer watchdog names blinds company over 14,000 in unpaid refunds
item.description: The Malta Competition and Consumer Affairs Authority said Portelli and Brincat Limited (C5467) owes 18 customers a combined 14,205.50 for faulty or undelivered blinds, having failed to refund them despite repeated warnings. The regulator said it issued the public statement in the interest of consumer protection and without prejudice to any further action that may be taken under the law, adding that the statement does not constitute a decision on any matter other than what was established in Consumer Claims Tribunal decisions.

item.title: Maritime lobby warns EU emissions trading is pushing business away from Malta
item.description: The Malta Maritime Forum said the EU Emissions Trading System as it stands is harming Europe and Malta and must be changed, describing it as an impractical system that creates unfair competition for European ports. The forum said shipping routes are diverting southwards without emissions falling, and that Europe is losing business, investment and maritime connectivity to North Africa, where the scheme applies differently or not at all. The MMF welcomed the prime ministers position at the European Political Community meeting in Ireland, where he echoed the criticism that the ETS was poorly designed and passed without broad consultation of the maritime industry.

item.title: Family of injured teenager warns of bogus fundraising collections
item.description: The family of 14-year-old Ben Caruana Rizzo, who suffered serious injuries when a boat he was on collided with rocks off Bahar iag two weeks ago, has warned of a scam involving people collecting money in his name. The family said no one has been authorised to conduct any fundraising and urged people to verify any collection with them first, after a shop owner in St Pauls Bay contacted them about someone going around local shops collecting money. His mother Yanika Rizzo said the matter was reported to police, and a police spokesperson confirmed a report was filed and investigations are under way.

item.title: Man bailed over alleged reading of wifes emails during separation case
item.description: A 38-year-old man was granted bail on Tuesday after being charged with accessing his wifes computer without consent during separation proceedings. He pleaded not guilty to six charges of computer misuse as well as psychological violence, stalking and harassment, and was accused of reading email exchanges between his wife and her lawyer. The defence asked for bail and the prosecution did not object, while requesting a protection order for the victim. Magistrate Caroline Farrugia Frendo granted bail under conditions including residence at an alternative address, weekly signing of the bail book, a 1,500 deposit and a 10,000 personal guarantee, and issued a protection order.

item.title: MDA seeks urgent fix to new rules on damage to neighbouring property
item.description: The Malta Development Association has asked the government, the Building and Construction Authority and the Chamber of Architects to urgently address concerns about the new Avoidance of Damage to Third Party Property (Amendment) Regulations (L.N. 305 of 2026). The MDA said it supports safe construction and protection for neighbouring properties, but the regulations must clearly define the responsibilities of developers, architects, contractors, subcontractors and specialist professionals, with clear boundaries between planning, design, supervision and execution. MDA president Michael Stivala said clear duties protect neighbours and give the industry certainty to operate responsibly.

item.title: Alfred Sant calls Budget 2027 TCN measures crazy and cack-handed
item.description: Former prime minister Alfred Sant said Finance Minister Clyde Caruana is right to raise the cost of imported labour but is doing it in a cack-handed way, calling the Budget 2027 measures targeting third-country nationals crazy. Speaking to Lawrence Gonzi, Sant said the measures target the poorest bracket rather than placing pressure on employers who recruit foreign workers, and argued they would drive TCN workers away and fuel racism and xenophobia. He said the real solution is mandatory trade union membership, a measure Labour proposed years ago and shelved after employer pushback.

item.title: Malta Police warn of scam texts claiming to be traffic fines
item.description: The Malta Police Force issued a warning about scam messages circulating that ask recipients to pay what appears to be a fine issued by Traffic Police. The messages are sent from a foreign number and include a suspicious link, and police confirmed the messages are a scam. Officers urged the public not to click any link even if the message appears to come from someone they know, never to enter personal or banking details, to verify the message through a separate channel, and to delete it.

item.title: Two Maltese surgeons trained abroad to strengthen colorectal service at Mater Dei
item.description: Health Minister Ian Borg told parliament that two Maltese surgeons are providing colorectal surgery at Mater Dei, having recently completed specialised training in centres in the United Kingdom, Italy and Ireland. Over the past year the two have trained in the use of robotics during bowel operations, and further training of a surgeon abroad is planned in the next two years. International guidelines require at least 20 bowel transplants a year for a centre to offer the service, with 30 recommended, and Malta currently falls short of that threshold.

item.title: Court of Appeal revokes permit for Cottonera development, calling Grade 1 protection absolute
item.description: Heritage NGO Din l-Art elwa has won a landmark legal victory after the Court of Appeal upheld its appeal and revoked the permit for a development on the Grade 1 scheduled Cottonera fortifications. The judgment, delivered on 16 November, confirmed that Grade 1 scheduling is not merely a presumption against development but an absolute prohibition on alterations to the appearance of such sites. The case concerned planning application PA/1012/24, which had authorised a 250 square metre structure and an underground reservoir on the glacis adjoining the Cottonera Lines, part of San Klement Park in abar. The Environment and Planning Review Tribunal had earlier sided with the authorities.

item.title: Five months jail for man who did not sign the bail book for six months
item.description: A 40-year-old man, Privilege Mupimhidzi, has been jailed for five months and fined 400 after admitting he did not sign the bail book or live at the address listed in his bail decree between October 2025 and April 2026. He told the court he had stopped signing because he was being threatened over his pending case. The prosecution said he should have reported any threats to the police, and the court found him guilty.

item.title: Malta 17th in EU gender equality index as work scores jump to third
item.description: Malta scored 59.6 out of 100 in the 2026 Gender Equality Index published by the European Institute for Gender Equality, ranking 17th among EU member states against an EU average of 64.5. The score rose 9.8 points since 2020 and 0.9 points in a year. Malta ranks third in the EU on equality at work with 77.6 points, up 4.8 points since 2025, and first on the measure covering the spread of women and men across different jobs. Women now hold 41% of managerial posts, above the EU average of 36%. The report also records a 37% gender pension gap, above the 24% EU average, and notes that women in Malta are 27% more likely than men to do daily housework while men are more likely to be in full-time employment.

item.title: Third country nationals paid over 20% of social security contributions
item.description: Figures tabled in parliament show third country nationals paid more than a fifth of Maltas social security contributions, with their income tax share rising to 12% of the total from 9.4% in 2023. Just under 81,000 TCNs were employed and declared taxable income in 2024, roughly a quarter of the workforce, and around 63,500 earned below the median wage of 20,800. The figures came in reply to a question by PN MP Miriana Calleja Testaferrata de Noto.

item.title: Maltese candidates say poor exam translations cost them EU jobs
item.description: PN MEP Peter Agius has raised with the European Commission the complaints of Maltese candidates sitting European Personnel Selection Office tests, who say Maltese-language exam papers contained grammatical errors, awkward sentence structures and unnatural wording. Agius asked the Commission to clarify its translation and proofreading procedures, to investigate the complaints and to have future exams reviewed by qualified Maltese-language experts, noting that Maltese is one of the EUs 24 official languages and that poor translations risk unequal treatment of Maltese applicants.

item.title: 42 court cases await judgment for five years or more
item.description: Justice Minister Clifton Grima told parliament that 42 cases presided over by magistrates or judges have been pending judgment for five years or more, with a further 40 pending for four to five years, against a backlog of 811 inquiries before magistrates and 760 before judges. Grima said the number of concluded magisterial inquiries rose to 1,392 in 2025 from 939 in 2024, and that 688 inquiries were concluded in the first ten months of this year.

item.title: WasteServ appeal succeeds but FOI decision still to be taken
item.description: The Court of Appeal has annulled the decision obliging WasteServ to hand over documents relating to the recruitment of former chief executive Richard Bilocca and lawyer Pearl Agius, after finding the appeals tribunal had not considered a key argument. The ruling does not mean the company has grounds to refuse the information, and the question of whether to comply has been returned to the tribunal to decide. The underlying access request by The Shift News dates from February 2023.

item.title: Momentum tells EU MEPs Malta faces crisis of transparency and institutional independence
item.description: Momentum leader Arnold Cassola and committee member Natasha Azzopardi told a European Parliament committee on Monday that Malta faces a deepening crisis of transparency, accountability and institutional independence. The LIBE delegation is in Malta on a rule of law mission prompted by the acquittal of Yorgen Fenech. The party raised the concealed 300-page population report commissioned in 2017, procedural and evidential errors leading to the collapse of cases involving prominent businessmen, freedom of information requests being ignored, concerns over the independence of the Police Commissioner and the Attorney General, reduced transparency on ministers assets and a weak opposition.

item.title: Paediatricians urge tougher tobacco and vaping rules as Malta holds out on EU taxes
item.description: The Maltese Paediatric Association has called on the government to introduce stronger tobacco and vaping control measures, including higher taxation, warning that youth vaping has become a growing epidemic driven by thousands of sweet flavourings, youth-targeted packaging and social media promotion. The association said nicotine dependence can be more than twice as high among e-cigarette users, and that young vapers are up to three times more likely to take up conventional cigarettes. The call follows a similar appeal by the Medical Association of Malta; Malta remains the sole member state holding out against the EU Tobacco Taxation Directive.

item.title: Seven people died by suicide in July, including a teenager
item.description: Home Affairs Minister Glenn Bedingfield told parliament that seven people died by suicide in July, the youngest aged 14 and the oldest 64, answering a question by PNs Graziella Attard Previ. Nineteen deaths by suicide were reported for the first six months of the year and 30 for the whole of last year, against a recent high of 35 in 2021 and a low of 21 in 2019. Experts caution that the numbers are too small to draw significant conclusions year on year.

item.title: Robert Abela marks 2,500 days as prime minister, overtaking Joseph Muscat
item.description: Robert Abela completed 2,500 days as prime minister on Tuesday, becoming the second longest-serving Labour prime minister in Maltas history, behind Dom Mintoff. Sworn in on 13 January 2020 after winning the Labour leadership, he has led the party through three general election victories, the most recent giving Labour a fourth consecutive mandate. Over his nearly seven years in office he has faced the COVID-19 pandemic, the war in Ukraine and the conflicts in the Middle East. Labour has also been through three Nationalist Party leaders since he took office.

item.title: Spearfisherman caught with undersized groupers tracked and arrested in Gozo
item.description: A spearfisherman seen catching undersized groupers in Mistra Bay was intercepted by police in Gozo after the Malta Rangers Unit alerted the Department of Fisheries and Aquaculture. The man left the site before fisheries officers arrived and headed towards irkewwa, where police stopped his vehicle as it came off the ferry at Marr. Officers confirmed he was in possession of undersized erna and confiscated the fish and his gear, with legal action expected. The minimum catch size for groupers is 45cm under Maltese and EU law, as undersized fish would not have had a chance to reproduce.

item.title: Employers association says Farrugia never served on the Development Bank board
item.description: The Malta Employers Association has disputed parliamentary information identifying its former director general Joseph Farrugia as a paid member of the Malta Development Bank board. The association said Farrugia was nominated but declined the position in order to continue representing employers on the Malta Council for Economic and Social Development, an unpaid role, and that his absence was verifiable on the banks website. The disputed 9,000 payment featured in figures cited by Labour MP Nigel Vella, who had claimed Farrugia earned around 20,000 a year from government board appointments in the dispute over the buffu remark.

item.title: 13,500 confiscated from bank accounts of deceased pensioner
item.description: The court ordered the confiscation of 13,558 from two bank accounts belonging to Lucy Grima, a pensioner from al Qormi who died in 2023 before criminal proceedings against her concluded. She had been accused of receiving money from unlicensed money-lending and banking activity, with police finding large cash deposits and handwritten ledgers during a search of her home in 2022. The court stressed that a gap in criminal proceedings does not allow authorities to automatically treat all of a persons property as proceeds of crime, and the heirs have contested the order.

item.title: Serial rapist jailed 18 years after pleading guilty to attacks on three massage therapists
item.description: Harona Conateh, a 34-year-old Gambian man, admitted terrorising, raping and attempting to rape three massage therapists in Sliema and Birkirkara between 22 June and 10 July 2024. He pleaded guilty to 17 charges under a plea-bargaining agreement, avoiding a jury trial, and received an 18-year sentence to be served consecutively with the eight-year term he was already serving for a separate attempted rape of another therapist. The court also convicted him of violently resisting arrest and injuring a police constable after he bolted from court during his arraignment in July 2024. In mitigation, the victims described repeated intimidation and abuse during the attacks.

item.title: Addolorata chapel shut after attempts to prise open tombs
item.description: The Chapel of the Confraternity of Mary, Mother of Sorrows inside the Addolorata Cemetery has been closed to the public after vandals tried to break into tombs by prising open the stone slabs covering them. Dominican friars said plaster surrounding the flagstones over several tombs had been removed, indicating repeated attempts to force the tombs open. The chapel, still used for burials, will now open only for authorised Masses and pilgrimages, with police and public health authorities informed. Prior Fr Aaron Zahra called the acts a disgrace to the dead and a public health risk.

Sources: Newsbook, Times of Malta, Malta Today, Lovin Malta

item.title: 20,000 people in Malta unaware they have diabetes
item.description: Endocrinologist Dr Miriam Giordano told RTK103 that international studies point to around 20,000 people in Malta who do not know they have diabetes, roughly one in ten residents. She explained that the condition often produces no symptoms and is picked up only through routine blood tests, and that type 2 diabetes is the most common form. She stressed the need for early detection, given the complications associated with prolonged high blood sugar.

item.title: Inquiry finds no single authority oversaw the Lourdes fireworks factory
item.description: The inquiry into the 1 June fireworks factory blast at Salini has exposed major gaps in regulatory oversight, with no single authority holding a complete picture of the factorys operations or a central record of its permits. Investigators found that inspectors routinely gave factories advance warning of visits and failed to flag breaches, while responsibility is split across the Armed Forces, police, the Fireworks Inspectorate Unit, the Explosives Committee, the Planning Authority and other agencies. The factory was destroyed in a massive explosion that damaged homes kilometres away, killed livestock and wrecked surrounding fields.

item.title: Child filmed hurling racist slurs at a foreign man on a bus
item.description: A video shared by Equality Minister Rosianne Cutajar on Tuesday shows a child directing racist slurs and insults at an Asian man on a packed bus, using the N-word and urging the man to hit him. The clip, first published by Malta Today, also shows the boy growling like a dog. Cutajar condemned the incident, saying racism often begins at home through the words and attitudes children grow up hearing, and warned that hate speech is a crime in Malta. The incident follows previous reports of children suspected of racist behaviour in Malta.
